As shown in Fig. 2 (a), the phase composition of 4Fe-1C alloy is Nbss, β-(Nb, X)5Si3 and γ-(Nb, X)5Si3. The γ-(Nb, X)5Si3 phase is mainly displayed as primary hexagonal block, while β-(Nb, X)5Si3 phase and Nbss phase form dendritic Nbss/β-(Nb, X)5Si3 eutectics.
The 5–3 types of silicides in 4Fe-1C alloy are mainly β-(Nb, X)5Si3 (JCPDS, 30–0875) phase, while γ-(Nb, X)5Si3 (JCPDS, 08–0422) phase accounts for a relatively low proportion.
The γ-(Nb, X)5Si3 phase is mainly displayed as primary hexagonal block, while β-(Nb, X)5Si3 phase and Nbss phase form dendritic Nbss/β-(Nb, X)5Si3 eutectics.

Besides, TiC particles with dark contrast are precipitated and distributed in the Nbss. Meanwhile, the amount of the TiC particles raises accordingly with the C content. It is interesting that TiC particles appear as discontinuous dendrite structures at the beginning (3 at% C), and then precipitate irregularly at 5 at% C
When addition of 6 at% Fe (Fig. 2 (d)), the microstructure changes significantly and a new silicide phase Nb4FeSi appears, which consists of four phases with Nbss, (Nb, X)5Si3, and Nb4FeSi.
The KQ value of the 4Fe-3C alloy reaches the highest with a mean of 14.49 MPa·m^1/2.
